title: Genesis Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 20.

questions.question: Where did Abraham dwell after journeying toward the south country?
questions.correctAnswer: Between Kadesh and Shur
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:1 states that Abraham journeyed toward the south country and dwelled between Kadesh and Shur.

questions.question: How did Abraham describe Sarah to Abimelech king of Gerar?
questions.correctAnswer: As his sister
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:2 says Abraham said of Sarah his wife, 'She is my sister.'

questions.question: Who took Sarah after Abraham said she was his sister?
questions.correctAnswer: Abimelech king of Gerar
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:2 states that Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.

questions.question: How did God communicate with Abimelech about Sarah?
options: Through an angel in the daytime
questions.correctAnswer: In a dream by night
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:3 tells us that God came to Abimelech in a dream by night.

questions.question: What did God say would happen to Abimelech if he kept Sarah?
options: He would be a dead man
questions.correctAnswer: He would be a dead man
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:3 says God told Abimelech, 'Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman which thou hast taken; for she is a man's wife.'

questions.question: True or False: Abimelech had already come near to Sarah when God warned him in the dream.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:4 states that Abimelech had not come near her when God warned him.

questions.question: What reason did Abimelech give for not touching Sarah?
options: He feared God and was innocent
He was away on a journey
questions.correctAnswer: He feared God and was innocent
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:5 shows Abimelech said, 'in the integrity of my heart and innocency of my hands have I done this.'

questions.question: True or False: God knew that Abimelech took Sarah with a guilty heart.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:6 says God knew Abimelech acted in the integrity of his heart and withheld him from sinning.

questions.question: What did God command Abimelech to do with Sarah?
questions.correctAnswer: Restore her to Abraham
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:7 commands Abimelech to restore Sarah to Abraham.

questions.question: What title did God give to Abraham in the dream to Abimelech?
questions.correctAnswer: Prophet
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:7 refers to Abraham as a prophet who will pray for Abimelech.

questions.question: True or False: Abimelech told all his servants about the dream and they were very afraid.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:8 states that Abimelech told his servants, and the men were sore afraid.

questions.question: What did Abimelech ask Abraham when he called him?
questions.correctAnswer: 'What have I offended thee?'
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:9 records Abimelech asking Abraham what he had done to bring a great sin upon him and his kingdom.

questions.question: What reason did Abraham give for saying Sarah was his sister?
options: He thought the fear of God was not in that place
He wanted to protect himself from strangers
He wanted to test Abimelech's faith
questions.correctAnswer: He thought the fear of God was not in that place
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:11 says Abraham thought surely the fear of God was not in that place, so they might slay him for Sarah's sake.

questions.question: In what order did these events happen in Genesis 20? 1) Abimelech took Sarah 2) God warned Abimelech in a dream 3) Abraham said Sarah was his sister 4) Abimelech restored Sarah to Abraham. Which came first?
options: Abraham said Sarah was his sister
God warned Abimelech in a dream
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham said Sarah was his sister
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:2 shows Abraham first said Sarah was his sister, then Abimelech took her, God warned Abimelech in a dream (verse 3), and finally Abimelech restored Sarah (verse 14).

questions.question: True or False: Abraham admitted that Sarah was his half-sister, being the daughter of his father but not of his mother.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:12 states that Sarah was the daughter of Abraham's father but not of his mother.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Genesis 20:7, what will happen if Abimelech does not restore Sarah to Abraham?
options: He and all that are his will surely die
He will be banished from the kingdom
He will be struck with blindness
questions.correctAnswer: He and all that are his will surely die
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:7 warns Abimelech that if he does not restore Sarah to Abraham, he and all that belong to him will surely die, showing the seriousness of obeying God's command.

questions.question: In Genesis 20:8, what was the reaction of Abimelech's servants after he told them about the dream from God?
questions.correctAnswer: They were sore afraid
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:8 states that after Abimelech told his servants about God's warning, the men were sore afraid, emphasizing the fear and respect for God's message among them.

questions.question: How did Abimelech confront Abraham in Genesis 20:9 regarding the taking of Sarah?
options: He accused Abraham of bringing a great sin and offending him
He blessed Abraham for his honesty
He asked Abraham to leave the land immediately
He ignored the situation and said nothing
questions.correctAnswer: He accused Abraham of bringing a great sin and offending him
questions.explanation: In Genesis 20:9, Abimelech confronted Abraham by saying he brought a great sin upon him and his kingdom, showing that Abimelech was upset by the deception and its consequences.

questions.question: What question did Abimelech ask Abraham in Genesis 20:10?
options: What sawest thou, that thou hast done this thing?
Why did you flee from me?
Who told you to come here?
questions.correctAnswer: What sawest thou, that thou hast done this thing?
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:10 records Abimelech asking Abraham what he saw that caused him to commit the act of saying Sarah was his sister, seeking to understand Abraham's motivation.

questions.question: According to Genesis 20:11, why did Abraham say he claimed Sarah was his sister?
options: Because he thought the fear of God was not in that place and he feared for his life
Because Sarah told him to do so
Because he wanted to deceive Abimelech
Because he was ashamed of Sarah
questions.correctAnswer: Because he thought the fear of God was not in that place and he feared for his life
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:11 explains Abraham's reasoning: he believed the people there did not fear God and would kill him to take Sarah, so he protected himself by calling her his sister.

questions.question: What relationship did Abraham clarify about Sarah in Genesis 20:12?
options: She was his half-sister, daughter of his father but not of his mother
She was not related to him at all
questions.correctAnswer: She was his half-sister, daughter of his father but not of his mother
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:12 clarifies that Sarah was Abraham's half-sister, sharing the same father but different mothers, which adds context to his claim that she was his sister.

questions.question: How does Genesis 20:7 teach about the importance of obedience to God's command in practical Christian living?
options: It shows that disobedience can bring severe consequences, including death
It indicates that God is lenient with disobedience
It suggests that obedience is optional
It implies that God does not intervene in human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that disobedience can bring severe consequences, including death
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:7 warns of death as a consequence for not restoring Sarah, teaching that obedience to God's commands is crucial and disobedience can lead to serious results.

questions.question: What practical lesson about integrity is demonstrated in Abimelech's response in Genesis 20:5?
options: He acted with innocence and integrity, unaware of wrongdoing
He was indifferent to moral concerns
questions.correctAnswer: He acted with innocence and integrity, unaware of wrongdoing
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:5 shows Abimelech insisting he acted with integrity and innocence, highlighting the value of a clear conscience and honest intentions in Christian conduct.

questions.question: In Genesis 20:17, what was the result of Abraham's prayer for Abimelech and his household?
options: God healed them and they bore children
They were exiled from the land
questions.correctAnswer: God healed them and they bore children
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:17 shows that Abraham prayed and God healed Abimelech and his household, enabling them to have children, illustrating the power of intercessory prayer and God's mercy.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 20:18, God had closed up all the wombs in Abimelech's household because of Sarah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:18 explicitly states that God had shut the wombs of Abimelech's household because of Sarah, showing divine intervention due to the situation.

questions.question: Based on Genesis 20:13, why did Abraham instruct Sarah to say he was her brother?
options: To protect himself during their travels in unfamiliar places
questions.correctAnswer: To protect himself during their travels in unfamiliar places
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:13 shows Abraham's strategy to ensure his safety by having Sarah say he was her brother, reflecting his fear of being harmed for her sake in new places.

questions.question: What does Genesis 20:16 reveal about Abimelech's attitude toward Sarah after the incident?
options: He gave her brother a thousand pieces of silver as a covering for the offense
He ignored her and sent her away
He demanded a ransom for her release
questions.correctAnswer: He gave her brother a thousand pieces of silver as a covering for the offense
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:16 records Abimelech giving Abraham silver as a covering for the offense, showing his acknowledgment of the wrong and his attempt to make amends.

questions.question: True or False: Abimelech had lain with Sarah before God warned him in a dream, according to Genesis 20:4.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:4 explicitly states that Abimelech had not come near Sarah, indicating he had not sinned with her before God warned him.

questions.question: How does Genesis 20:6 demonstrate God's recognition of human integrity?
options: God acknowledged Abimelech acted with a pure heart and withheld him from sin
questions.correctAnswer: God acknowledged Abimelech acted with a pure heart and withheld him from sin
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:6 shows God recognizing Abimelech's innocent intentions and preventing him from sinning, highlighting God's justice and mercy toward integrity.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 20:14 shows Abimelech giving livestock and servants to Abraham as a gesture of goodwill after restoring Sarah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:14 states that Abimelech gave Abraham sheep, oxen, and servants, demonstrating generosity and reconciliation after the misunderstanding.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 20.

questions.question: What reason did Abraham give for calling Sarah his sister instead of his wife when speaking to Abimelech?
options: He feared being killed because of her
He wanted to test Abimelech's faith
He wanted to keep his family lineage secret
questions.correctAnswer: He feared being killed because of her
questions.explanation: Abraham said he thought the fear of God was not in that place and that they would kill him for his wife's sake (Genesis 20:11).

questions.question: According to Genesis 20, what relation was Sarah to Abraham besides being his wife?
questions.correctAnswer: She was his half-sister
questions.explanation: Abraham explained Sarah was the daughter of his father but not of his mother, making her his half-sister (Genesis 20:12).

questions.question: What did God do to Abimelech's household because of Sarah?
options: Closed up all the wombs preventing conception
questions.correctAnswer: Closed up all the wombs preventing conception
questions.explanation: God had fast closed up all the wombs of Abimelech's house because of Sarah, Abraham's wife (Genesis 20:18).

questions.question: What did Abimelech give to Abraham after realizing the truth about Sarah?
questions.correctAnswer: Sheep, oxen, menservants, and womenservants
questions.explanation: Abimelech gave Abraham sheep, oxen, and servants, and restored Sarah to him (Genesis 20:14).

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'thousand pieces of silver' Abimelech gave to Sarah?
options: It served as a covering of the eyes, symbolizing a public acknowledgment and reproof
It was a bride price for Sarah's hand
It was a ransom to release Abraham
It was a gift to celebrate a festival
questions.correctAnswer: It served as a covering of the eyes, symbolizing a public acknowledgment and reproof
questions.explanation: Abimelech said the silver was to Sarah as a covering of the eyes to all with her, indicating a public vindication and reproof (Genesis 20:16).

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently seen in the narrative of Abraham calling Sarah his sister and the subsequent divine intervention?
options: Inclusio framing the chapter with Abraham's deception and God's protection
Parallelism between Abraham and Abimelech's actions
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the chapter with Abraham's deception and God's protection
questions.explanation: The chapter begins and ends with Abraham's deceptive claim and God's protective intervention, creating an inclusio structure (Genesis 20:2 and 20:18).

questions.question: In the context of Genesis 20, what does the Hebrew root of the word 'integrity' (used in verse 6) imply about Abimelech's actions?
options: Sincerity and innocence of heart and hands
questions.correctAnswer: Sincerity and innocence of heart and hands
questions.explanation: God acknowledges Abimelech’s actions were done with integrity, meaning sincere and innocent, as stated in Genesis 20:6.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s protective intervention seen in Genesis 20?
options: Hebrews 11:11-12 highlighting Abraham’s faith and God’s promise
Matthew 1:18-25 describing Joseph's divine warning in a dream
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 1:18-25 describing Joseph's divine warning in a dream
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:18-25 parallels God's intervention through dreams to protect the chosen family, as in Genesis 20:3-7.

questions.question: How does Genesis 20 develop the theme of God’s covenantal protection introduced earlier in Genesis?
options: By showing God prevents sin from disrupting His promises to Abraham
By allowing Abimelech to take Sarah
questions.correctAnswer: By showing God prevents sin from disrupting His promises to Abraham
questions.explanation: God intervenes to protect Sarah and Abraham’s covenant, preventing Abimelech from sinning against God’s plan (Genesis 20:6-7).

questions.question: True or False: Abimelech immediately suspected Abraham was lying when he claimed Sarah was his sister.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Abimelech accepted Abraham’s claim until God revealed the truth to him in a dream (Genesis 20:5-7).

questions.question: True or False: Abraham's instruction to Sarah to say he was her brother was intended as a protective kindness.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Abraham called this a kindness Sarah should show him to protect him wherever they traveled (Genesis 20:13).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly shows a patriarch calling his wife his sister to protect himself?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 12:10-20 (Abraham in Egypt)
questions.explanation: Genesis 12:10-20 recounts Abraham also calling Sarah his sister in Egypt out of fear for his life, paralleling Genesis 20 (Genesis 12:11-13).

questions.question: What was Abimelech's reaction after God revealed the truth to him in the dream?
options: He feared and told his servants all that had happened
He ignored the warning and kept Sarah
questions.correctAnswer: He feared and told his servants all that had happened
questions.explanation: Abimelech rose early, called his servants, and told them, causing fear among them (Genesis 20:8).

questions.question: What role did Abraham’s prophetic prayer play after the events with Abimelech?
options: It led to God healing Abimelech and his household, allowing them to bear children
It caused a drought in Gerar
questions.correctAnswer: It led to God healing Abimelech and his household, allowing them to bear children
questions.explanation: Abraham prayed and God healed Abimelech’s household, reversing the barrenness caused by the Lord (Genesis 20:17).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'covering of the eyes' in Genesis 20:16 metaphorically signify in the cultural context of the ancient Near East?
options: A public acknowledgment of innocence and protection from shame
questions.correctAnswer: A public acknowledgment of innocence and protection from shame
questions.explanation: The silver was given to Sarah as a covering of the eyes, meaning it was a token of honor and protection against slander in the ancient Near East (Genesis 20:16).

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Genesis 20:3, what was the divine warning given to Abimelech in his dream?
options: He was going to lose his kingdom
He was about to become blind
He was but a dead man for taking a married woman
He would be exiled from Gerar
questions.correctAnswer: He was but a dead man for taking a married woman
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:3 states that God warned Abimelech in a dream, 'Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman which thou hast taken; for she is a man's wife.' This reveals God's protective justice over marriage.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by God's intervention to prevent Abimelech from sinning against Him despite Abimelech's ignorance (Genesis 20:6)?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine providence and grace
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:6 reveals God's providence and grace, as He withheld Abimelech from sinning knowingly, demonstrating God's sovereign protection over human actions.

questions.question: How does Abraham explain his deception regarding Sarah's identity in Genesis 20:11-12, and what does this reveal about human fear and sin?
options: He expected the king to honor God's covenant
He feared for his life because he thought there was no fear of God in that place and claimed Sarah as his sister
He wanted to test God's protection over Sarah
He was following a divine command
questions.correctAnswer: He feared for his life because he thought there was no fear of God in that place and claimed Sarah as his sister
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:11-12 shows Abraham's fear led him to deception, reflecting human weakness and distrust in hostile environments, revealing the reality of sin even in godly men.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His healing Abimelech and his household after Abraham's prayer, as recorded in Genesis 20:17?
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and healing power
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:17 highlights God's mercy and healing power as He responds to Abraham's intercession by restoring fertility to Abimelech's household.

questions.question: In Genesis 20:7, God calls Abraham a prophet. What does this title signify in the context of this chapter?
options: Abraham has the ability to foretell the future only
Abraham is a mediator who can pray for others and intercede
Abraham is a king over Gerar
Abraham is a priest who offers sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham is a mediator who can pray for others and intercede
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:7 shows Abraham's prophetic role includes intercession, as God commands the restoration of Sarah and promises life upon Abraham's prayer, indicating mediation between God and man.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Genesis 20:4 and 20:6 provide about human innocence and divine knowledge?
options: Humans can be innocent, but God fully knows their hearts and intentions
Human innocence is irrelevant to God
questions.correctAnswer: Humans can be innocent, but God fully knows their hearts and intentions
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:4 shows Abimelech's innocence ('had not come near her'), and Genesis 20:6 confirms God knows the integrity of his heart, revealing divine omniscience surpassing human understanding.

questions.question: How does Genesis 20:1-2 introduce the narrative's setting and Abraham's initial action, and what does this suggest about human vulnerability even in God's plan?
options: Abraham settled in a safe city and trusted God fully
Abraham journeyed and sojourned in Gerar, but declared Sarah his sister, showing human caution bordering on deception
Abraham built a temple to God immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham journeyed and sojourned in Gerar, but declared Sarah his sister, showing human caution bordering on deception
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:1-2 sets the scene and reveals Abraham’s human vulnerability and fear, which led to deception despite God's overarching plan.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical significance does Genesis 20:18 reveal about God's intervention in human fertility and covenant promises?
options: God closed all wombs in Abimelech’s household to protect Sarah's marriage and uphold His covenant with Abraham
Fertility was unrelated to covenant promises
God's promises are conditional on human works
questions.correctAnswer: God closed all wombs in Abimelech’s household to protect Sarah's marriage and uphold His covenant with Abraham
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:18 shows God's sovereign control over fertility as a means to protect His covenant promises through Sarah, prefiguring the covenantal theme of divine intervention to preserve the Messiah's lineage.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the story of Abraham deceiving Abimelech is evidence of moral failure in God's chosen patriarch. What does Genesis 20:11-13 actually teach about Abraham's motives and human sinfulness?
options: Abraham was completely righteous without fault
Abraham acted out of fear due to perceived lack of fear of God in that place, revealing human frailty and the reality of sin even in the godly
Abraham was deliberately trying to sin
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham acted out of fear due to perceived lack of fear of God in that place, revealing human frailty and the reality of sin even in the godly
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:11-13 shows Abraham’s fear motivated his deception, illustrating that God’s people are still prone to sin, aligning with doctrines of human depravity and the need for divine grace.

questions.question: How does Abimelech’s response in Genesis 20:9-10 reflect the human recognition of sin and accountability before God?
options: Abimelech confronts Abraham, recognizing a great sin has been brought upon his kingdom
Abimelech praises Abraham for his wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Abimelech confronts Abraham, recognizing a great sin has been brought upon his kingdom
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:9-10 shows Abimelech’s awareness of wrongdoing and accountability, emphasizing human moral responsibility even when sin is committed unknowingly.

questions.question: What does Genesis 20:16 reveal about social customs and the concept of restitution in the ancient Near East?
options: Money was never used in social transactions
Abimelech gave Sarah a covering of the eyes through a gift of silver to her brother, signifying a form of compensation or restitution
Restitution was only spiritual, not material
Kings did not engage in gifts or compensation
questions.correctAnswer: Abimelech gave Sarah a covering of the eyes through a gift of silver to her brother, signifying a form of compensation or restitution
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:16 shows the social and legal custom of compensating a wronged party, reflecting the seriousness of the offense and the restoration of honor.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God's mercy and human obedience is taught by Genesis 20:7 and Genesis 20:17?
options: God does not respond to prayer
God requires obedience and responds mercifully to intercessory prayer, preserving life and healing
Prayer is only for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: God requires obedience and responds mercifully to intercessory prayer, preserving life and healing
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:7 commands restoration of Sarah and promises life upon Abraham’s prayer; Genesis 20:17 shows God healing Abimelech’s household, teaching divine mercy tied to obedience and prayer.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by His direct communication to Abimelech in a dream (Genesis 20:3)?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:3 reveals God's attribute of Revelation, as He directly communicates warnings to mortals through dreams, making known His will and moral law.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Genesis 20 contribute to the broader biblical theme of God's faithfulness to His covenant despite human failings?
options: It shows God abandoning His promises due to Abraham's sin
It illustrates God's protection of the covenant line through Sarah despite Abraham's deception and human sin
It indicates God changes His mind frequently
It focuses only on Abraham's faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's protection of the covenant line through Sarah despite Abraham's deception and human sin
questions.explanation: Genesis 20 demonstrates God's faithfulness in preserving Sarah and the covenant lineage despite Abraham's fear-driven deception, reinforcing the theme of divine grace over human weakness.

questions.question: What synthesis of Abraham’s fear and God’s protective intervention is evident when combining Genesis 20:11 and Genesis 20:6?
options: Human fear always leads to sin without exception
Although Abraham feared for his life and sinned, God’s grace prevented the sin from fully occurring
God punished Abraham severely for his fear
God ignored Abraham’s fear and allowed harm
questions.correctAnswer: Although Abraham feared for his life and sinned, God’s grace prevented the sin from fully occurring
questions.explanation: Genesis 20:11 shows Abraham’s fear-driven deception; Genesis 20:6 reveals God’s grace in withholding Abimelech from touching Sarah, illustrating divine mercy in human failure.
